The test image shows a whole plant view with one central plant that is severely affected — brown/dead leaves still attached, interveinal yellowing visible on adjacent leaves, while surrounding plants remain green. This pattern of selective plant death with interveinal chlorosis/necrosis is characteristic of several diseases. Top candidates: Sudden Death Syndrome, Phytophthora, Brown Stem Rot.

Let me check a reference image for Sudden Death Syndrome.

The reference SDS image shows patches of yellowing/dying plants in a field with interveinal chlorosis — consistent with what I see in the test image. The test image shows:
- A single plant that has died (brown, dried leaves still attached)
- Interveinal chlorosis/yellowing visible on adjacent/surrounding leaves
- Surrounding plants remain green and healthy
- The "islands" of death pattern in a field

This strongly matches **Sudden Death Syndrome**: interveinal chlorosis/necrosis with leaves dying while petioles remain, plant death in isolated spots among healthy plants.
